title: What training do assisted living facility staff need in Texas?
description: Texas ALF staff training under 26 TAC 553.253: 4-hour orientation, 16 hours supervised attendant training, 6 hours a year, and 2024 Alzheimer's rules.
shortAnswer: In Texas, every assisted living facility staff member must complete 4 hours of orientation before taking on any duties, and attendants then need 16 hours of on-the-job supervision and training, under 26 Texas Administrative Code 553.253. Direct care staff need 6 documented hours of education every year, including competency-based fall prevention and behavior management. Managers need a 24-hour course and 12 hours of annual continuing education, and 2024 rules add dementia training.
keyTakeaways: All staff complete 4 hours of orientation before assuming any job responsibilities, covering abuse and neglect reporting, confidentiality, universal precautions, residents' rights and emergency procedures.
Attendants complete 16 hours of on-the-job supervision and training within their first 16 hours of employment following orientation.
Direct care staff complete 6 documented hours of education each year from their hire date, including 1 hour of fall prevention and 1 hour of behavior management, both competency-based.

Managers complete a 24-hour assisted living management course by the first anniversary of employment, including 8 hours on the standards in the first 3 months, then 12 hours of continuing education each year.

Since September 12, 2024, facilities that are not Alzheimer's certified but serve residents with dementia must give personal care staff 4 hours of competency-evaluated dementia training before they provide personal care.
regulator: Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC)
appliesTo: Assisted living facilities licensed by HHSC under 26 TAC Chapter 553, Type A and Type B, small and large
All facility staff members, with additional requirements for attendants and direct care staff
Licensed nurses, certified nurse aides and certified medication aides employed by the facility
Facility managers, and managers or supervisors of certified Alzheimer's facilities or units

sections.heading: Which Texas rules set assisted living training requirements?

blocks.text: 26 Texas Administrative Code Chapter 553, Licensing Standards for Assisted Living Facilities, administered by the Texas Health and Human Services Commission (HHSC). The core training rule is [26 TAC 553.253](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/26-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-553-253), Employee Qualifications and Training. Alzheimer's training is in [553.254](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/26-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-553-254) and [553.255](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/26-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-553-255) for all facilities and in Subchapter F, including [553.303](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/26-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-553-303), for certified Alzheimer's facilities. HHSC lists Chapter 553 as the governing rule on its [assisted living facilities provider page](https://www.hhs.texas.gov/providers/long-term-care-providers/assisted-living-facilities-alf).

This page reflects the rule text as at November 2026, including the September 12, 2024 amendments that added 553.254. Rule text was read on the Legal Information Institute's Texas Administrative Code mirror, which is updated quarterly, so confirm against the Texas Secretary of State's official Texas Administrative Code before relying on it.

sections.heading: What training must new Texas assisted living staff complete?

blocks.text: Four hours of orientation for everyone, then 16 hours of supervised training for attendants. Under 553.253(d), the facility must document that staff are competent to provide personal care before assuming responsibilities.

blocks.caption: 26 TAC 553.253(d)(1) and (2): initial training
head: Requirement
Who
When
Minimum content
rows: Reporting abuse and neglect; confidentiality of resident information; universal precautions; conditions to report to the manager; residents' rights; emergency and evacuation procedures
Within the first 16 hours of employment following orientation

Assistance with activities of daily living; residents' health conditions; accident and injury prevention; emergency first aid such as the Heimlich maneuver and responses to falls, lacerations and sudden changes; managing disruptive behavior; behavior management and alternatives to restraint; fall prevention

blocks.text: Because attendant training is defined as the first 16 hours of work after orientation, the attendant's first shifts are themselves the training period and must be supervised and documented. See [how to train frontline and deskless workers](/guides/how-to-train-frontline-and-deskless-workers) for practical delivery approaches.

sections.heading: How much annual training do direct care staff need in Texas?

blocks.text: Six documented hours a year, counted from each employee's hire date, under 553.253(d)(3). At least 1 hour must be fall prevention and 1 hour behavior management, such as preventing aggressive behavior, de-escalation, reducing restraint use and alternatives to restraints. Training on these two subjects must be competency-based, and subject matter must address the unique needs of the facility.

The rule suggests further topics, including resident dignity and choice, communication with residents with hearing, visual or cognitive impairment, common physical and mental disorders such as dementia, depression and stroke, cardiopulmonary resuscitation, common medications and psychotropic side effects, understanding mental illness, conflict resolution, and community resources.

Facilities employing licensed nurses, certified nurse aides or certified medication aides must also give them annual in-service training appropriate to their jobs under 553.253(d)(4), drawn from areas such as geriatric communication, physical and psychological changes of aging, geriatric pharmacology, common geriatric emergencies, mental disorders, and legal and ethical issues including advance directives and guardianship. For assessment design, see [how to design competency assessments](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: What training do Texas assisted living managers need?

blocks.text: A 24-hour management course and 12 hours of annual continuing education. Under 553.253(a)(2), the course must cover the assisted living standards, resident characteristics including dementia, resident assessment, management principles, food and nutrition services, federal law with emphasis on the Americans with Disabilities Act, community resources, ethics and financial management.

items: Eight hours of training on the assisted living standards must be completed within the first three months of employment.

The full 24 hours must be completed by the first anniversary of employment as manager, through structured classes, correspondence courses, videos, distance learning or off-site courses from academic institutions, assisted living corporations or recognized organizations. Facility in-services do not count.

Managers need 12 hours of continuing education every year, covering at least two listed areas such as residents' rights and abuse, management principles, resident needs, accounting and budgeting, first aid, or federal employment and accessibility law. The 24-hour course meets this in the first year.
A manager who moves between licensed facilities with a break of no more than 30 days is exempt from repeating the 24-hour course.

blocks.text: Managers or unit supervisors of certified Alzheimer's facilities need 6 hours of annual continuing education in dementia care under [553.301](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/texas/26-Tex-Admin-Code-SS-553-301). HHSC publishes a provider list of approved manager courses on its provider page.

sections.heading: What Alzheimer's training applies to Texas assisted living facilities?

blocks.text: It depends on whether the facility is Alzheimer's certified. Every facility must adopt and enforce a written policy under 553.255 requiring direct care employees who serve residents with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder to complete training covering symptoms of dementia, stages of Alzheimer's disease, person-centered behavioral interventions and communication.

items: Non-certified facilities serving residents with dementia, 553.254 (effective September 12, 2024): personal care staff complete 4 hours of training and pass a competency-based evaluation before performing personal care, then 2 hours of continuing education on best practices. Managers complete 4 hours with a competency-based evaluation on a wider list including care planning and staffing, then 2 hours of annual continuing education. Non-direct staff such as housekeeping, front desk and maintenance complete training and pass an evaluation on dementia basics, person-centered care and communication.

Certified Alzheimer's facilities, 553.303: all staff complete 4 hours of dementia-specific orientation before assuming any duties; attendants complete 16 hours of supervised on-the-job training after orientation covering dementia-specific topics; and attendants complete 12 hours of Alzheimer's in-service education every year, including 1 competency-based hour on behavior management, fall prevention or restraint alternatives.

blocks.text: Under 553.254(e) and (f), the facility must give each staff member a training completion certificate and keep records, and a staff member who transfers to another facility within a two-year lapse of employment does not need to repeat the training.

sections.heading: What training evidence should a Texas facility keep?

blocks.text: HHSC surveyors check that training happened before the relevant duty began, so dates matter as much as content. For manager training, 553.253(a)(2)(A)(iii) requires evidence on file showing content, hours, dates and provider. The table below is an illustrative register.

Compare the [Florida](/regulations/florida-assisted-living-core-training) and [California](/regulations/california-assisted-living-rcfe-staff-training) regimes, which set higher initial hours for direct care staff.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each Chapter 553 requirement to the duty it gates, such as any duties, personal care, or managing, and to the competency evidence the rule names. Facilities that change Alzheimer's certification status can see which requirements switch from 553.254 to Subchapter F. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can Texas assisted living orientation be done after a new hire starts work?
faqs.a: No. 26 TAC 553.253(d)(1) requires all staff members to complete four hours of orientation before assuming any job responsibilities. Attendants then complete 16 hours of on-the-job supervision and training within the first 16 hours of employment following orientation.

faqs.q: When is the annual 6-hour training due for Texas assisted living staff?
faqs.a: It is counted from each employee's hire date rather than the calendar year. 553.253(d)(3) requires six documented hours of education annually, based on each employee's hire date, including one competency-based hour each on fall prevention and behavior management.

faqs.q: Do facilities without Alzheimer's certification need dementia training?
faqs.a: Yes, if they provide personal care to residents with Alzheimer's disease or a related disorder. Since September 12, 2024, 553.254 requires 4 hours of training with a competency-based evaluation before personal care, then continuing education, and separate training for managers and non-direct staff.

faqs.q: Can facility in-services count toward the Texas manager's 24-hour course?
faqs.a: No. 553.253(a)(2)(A)(ii) states that the 24-hour requirement may not be met through in-services at the facility. It may be met through structured classes, correspondence courses, training videos, distance learning or off-site courses provided by academic institutions, assisted living corporations or recognized organizations.

factCheck.claim: 553.253(d)(1): 4 hours orientation before any job responsibilities, six listed topics; (d)(2) attendants 16 hours on-the-job supervision and training within first 16 hours after orientation, seven topics; (d)(3) 6 documented hours annually by hire date, 1 hour fall prevention and 1 hour behavior management, competency-based; (d)(4) annual in-service for nurses, CNAs, CMAs. Adopted eff. 8/31/2021 (46 TexReg 5017).

553.253(a)(2): 24-hour management course, 8 hours on standards within first three months, not via facility in-services, by first anniversary; evidence on file of content, hours, dates, provider; 30-day transfer exemption; (a)(3) 12 hours annual CE incl. at least two listed areas.

553.254 (eff. 9/12/2024, 49 TexReg 7047): non-certified facilities; personal care staff 4 hours plus competency-based evaluation before personal care, then 2 hours CE; managers 4 hours plus evaluation then 2 hours annual CE; non-direct staff training and evaluation; certificates; two-year lapse portability.
553.255: written policy requiring dementia training for direct care employees covering symptoms, stages, person-centered behavioral interventions, communication; amended eff. 9/12/2024.

553.303: certified Alzheimer's facilities: 4 hours dementia-specific orientation for all staff before duties; attendants 16 hours on-the-job after orientation; attendants 12 hours annual Alzheimer's in-service with one competency-based hour. 553.301(b): manager or supervisor 6 hours annual dementia CE.
